Interactive Features:

  • Adjust the slider to expand the decoder stack and see sequential processing.
  • Hover or click any major architectural block to reveal its function in next-token prediction.
  • Click Trace Prediction to trace how the causal mask aggregates prefix context to predict the next token.

authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the architecture of an autoregressive transformer decoder, drawn as a horizontal left-to-right pipeline over a sequence of token positions. At the left, a vertical stack of word-embedding vectors represents the input sequence tokens: <start>, It, takes, great, courage, to, and let. These embeddings enter a large block labeled “Transformer with masked attention,” annotated (× K) to indicate K repeated decoder layers. Inside the transformer block, a lower-triangular masked-attention diagram shows that each token position can attend only to itself and earlier positions, preventing access to future tokens during next-token prediction. The block also shows residual/addition nodes and intermediate feature vectors that pass through the repeated masked-attention layers. At the right, each processed token representation feeds into a “Linear + softmax” block, producing a probability distribution over the vocabulary for the corresponding target token. The target-token labels shown on the far right are It, takes, great, courage, to, let, and yourself, illustrating shifted autoregressive training where the model predicts the next token at each position. This figure introduces the decoder-only transformer architecture for sequence generation, emphasizing causal masking and parallel next-token prediction across positions.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for K (number of decoder layers): expand the ×K repeated block to show K stacked masked-attention layers, or collapse it back to the compact ×K notation
- Click a processing block (Word embeddings, Transformer with masked attention, residual Add ⊕, Linear + softmax, or Probability of target token) to highlight it and display a tooltip describing its role in next-token prediction
- Animate the prediction of the target word “yourself”: trace the input prefix ending at “let” through the masked-attention block, residual additions, and final Linear + softmax layer to the output probability row labeled “yourself”

discrepancies: The '<start>' input token label is completely missing from the left side, likely swallowed by the browser as an unrecognized HTML/XML tag.
The '(×K)' label and horizontal ellipses ('· · ·') heavily collide with the lines entering the 'Linear + softmax' block.

The source figure represents the residual addition with a single '⊕' symbol and a vertical black line spanning all 7 paths, whereas the generated figure draws 7 separate '⊕' symbols without the vertical line.
The 7 blue feed-forward pills in the source figure are visually grouped by a vertical connecting line, which is absent in the generated figure.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure includes exceptional, highly pedagogical interactions that perfectly demonstrate causal masked attention, though it suffers from a missing tag label and a text collision.
action_items: Escape the first token as '<start>' so it correctly renders in the SVG text node instead of being parsed out as an empty tag.
Increase the horizontal gap between the Transformer block and the Linear block, or adjust the x-coordinates of the '(×K)' and '· · ·' labels to resolve their collision.
Add a vertical stroke connecting the 7 blue pills in the feed-forward layer to match the source figure's visual grouping.
Replace the 7 individual '⊕' symbols with a single '⊕' on the top path and a vertical line passing through all 7 paths to match the source's architectural shorthand.
